5a9ce647a34b32dddf096dd7f17697b44a5f5b0b.summary: A Google Threat Intelligence Group report on how government-backed APT and influence-operation actors from Iran, China, North Korea and Russia tried to use the Gemini assistant, mostly for research, coding help, translation and content creation. Google reports no novel AI capabilities and mostly unsuccessful jailbreak attempts. Iranian actors were the heaviest users, and APT42 focused on phishing. North Korean job research is assessed as likely tied to clandestine IT worker schemes.

hedges: The report says current LLMs on their own are unlikely to enable breakthrough capabilities for threat actors.
The report says it did not observe novel AI capabilities; its findings are limited to the dataset it analysed.
The report assesses that North Korean job-related Gemini usage is likely tied to clandestine IT worker efforts, while noting such research would be typical for any job seeker.
The report says the purpose of APT43's access to multiple public LLM tools is not clear; possible uses are described only as possibilities.
The report says it is not clear why Russian government-backed actors used Gemini so little; it offers several possible explanations.
The report says CopyCop likely used LLMs to generate content.
The report assesses with high confidence that North Korean cyber threat actors will continue to show interest in AI technologies.

5ad03e660c6312289bb7d76fc420484d5a1e3338.summary: A DataBreaches report (published 2025-08-08) relays claims from the ShinyHunters actor, speaking on Telegram. The claims include an extortion demand sent to Google after Google disclosed a breach, threats against Australian organisations including Qantas, and a stated focus on the USA, UK, Australia, CA and France. The report says it cannot confirm most of these claims. French police say they arrested the group's leader on June 23, but the report notes doubts about that arrest.
